articleTitle: Tight BER Bounds of MPSK Signals for the Shadowed Second Order Scattering Fading
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: The presented research assumes a problem of the M-PSK average bit error rate (ABER) calculation for the wireless communication system functioning in the presence of the second order scattering fading channel with fluctuating line-of-sight component. To evaluate ABER, numerically efficient exponential-mixture type tight approximations of the Gaussian Q-function were assumed and compared in terms of the relative error, which they provide. For the general exponential-mixture type approximation model, a closed-form expression of the ABER was derived and evaluated for the chosen (best) bound. Based on the obtained exact ABER expression, the closed-form asymptotic ABER (in the case of high signal-to-noise ratio) is derived. A numerical analysis proved the consistency of the analytical solution.

articleTitle: Cuprous Oxide Thin Films Deposited by Chemical Bath Deposition: Effect of Temperature and TEA
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This study presents the synthesis of the Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O thin films by chemical bath deposition. The effect of temperature and the amount of triethanolamine (TEA) on the film's structural, optical, and electrical properties is studied. It is found that regardless of the amount of TEA, as the deposit temperature increases, thicker films are formed with a better-defined morphology and larger particle size. This causes the structural disorder to decrease and consequently, reduces the conductivity, and then increases the Bandgap value. The increase in TEA causes a greater complexation of the copper ion, which implies that the reaction is slower, and consequently, the oxide precipitates more slowly, and a film with more controlled growth is formed, resulting in thicker films with more homogeneous morphology, and larger particle size. It is noteworthy that thicknesses greater than one micron were achieved, which is remarkable for its applications in diverse fields. This opens the possibility of using this material through this technique in solar technology such as photovoltaics.

articleTitle: Bearing Vibrations Classification for Failure Detection with Machine Learning Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: In this work, we have utilized Artificial Intelligence for the extraction and recognition of mechanical vibration information, which was obtained by electronic instruments, to identify whether a mechanical device is healthy or presents some kind of failure. We focused on building a Deep Autoencoder architecture (an unsupervised architecture), training the model, and extracting the internal structural information, also known as clustering. Lastly, the compressed information (as most Autoencoders have a reduced input representation in the internal structure) is classified into two classes using the supervised Extreme Learning Machine model.We utilized a dataset provided by Case Western Reserve University on its website. The signals were measured by sampling an accelerometer at 12kS/s, radially placed on a bearing. The measurements were taken for four cases, namely: the first case encompassed vibrational signals from a healthy bearing, and the other three cases involved bearings with intentionally induced failures in the inner race, outer race, and the ball, respectively.We developed this intelligent system using Python within the Jupyter environment, which operates in conjunction with the TensorFlow and Keras frameworks. We also successfully trained the model.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation of a New Double-Absorber Lead-free Perovskite Solar Cell via SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This work investigates the effectiveness of a lead-free perovskite solar cell based on MAGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/CsSnGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> double-absorber structure engineering and an optimized band alignment design. Moreover, in this study we have explored different electron and hole transport layers (ETL and HTL) and their impact on the solar cell performances using accurate numerical simulations. Also, using the SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O as ETL and HTL, respectively, provides excellent solar cell performances. Further, optimizations in terms of both absorber layer thicknesses, energy band alignment and defect density have also been performed. Besides, the obtained optimum parameters have been implemented in the proposed lead-free perovskite solar cell structure (FTO/ SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> (electron transport layer) / MAGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-CsSnGeI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> double-absorber layer/Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O (hole transport layers)/Au). The performance parameters provided by the proposed structure are compared with the already existing perovskite solar cells, where remarkable enhancements in the device performances were achieved with power conversion efficiency (PCE)= 33.57%, open-circuit voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>)=1.32V, short-circuit current ( J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>)= 28.11 mA/cm2 and Fill factor (FF)= 90.37 %. Therefore, these findings open the perspective for developing alternative efficient lead-free perovskite solar cells, which are highly suitable for newly emerging non toxic and low-cost thin-film photovoltaic applications.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of a DC servomechanism using a Robust Least Squares Algorithm with Variable Forgetting Factor
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This work presents a comparative analysis between two online parameter identification algorithms, namely the Robust Least-Squares and the Robust Least Squares with Variable Forgetting Factor, and the standard offline Least Squares algorithm. These algorithms are employed for estimating the parameters of the model of a DC servomechanism which is the main component of a low-cost experimental platform. The algorithms are tested using real-time data.

Author Keywords: online identification and low-cost experimental platform

articleTitle: Outage performance of the α-Beaulieu-Xie Shadowed Fading Channel Model
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: The research presents the closed-form outage analysis of the newly presented α-modification of the shadowed Beaulieu-Xie fading model for wireless communications. For the considered channel, the closed-form analytical expressions for the outage probability (including its upper and lower bounds), raw moments, amount of fading, and channel quality estimation indicator are derived. The carried out thorough numerical simulation and analysis demonstrates strong agreement with the presented closed-form solutions and illustrates the relationship between the outage probability and channel parameters.

articleTitle: Settling Time Reduction by Open-Loop Control Based on Parametric Anti-Resonance
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Parametric anti-resonance is a phenomenon that occurs in systems with at least two degrees of freedom; this can be achieved by periodically exciting some parameters of the system. The effect of this properly tuned periodicity is to increase the dissipation in the system, which leads to a raising in the effective damping of vibrations. This contribution presents the design of an open-loop control to reduce the settling time using the anti-resonance concept. The control signal consists of a quasi-periodic signal capable of transferring the system’s oscillations from one mode to another mode of the system. The general averaging technique is used to characterize the dynamics, particularly the so-called slow dynamics of motion. With this analysis, the control signal is designed for the potential application of a microelectromechanical sensor arrangement; for this specific example, up to 96.8% reduction of settling time is achieved.

articleTitle: Orthogonal Quad-Port Wearable MIMO Antenna for Sub-6GHz 5G and WLAN/Wi-Max/Wi-Fi Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: An orthogonal dual/quad port multi-in multi-out (MIMO) antenna configuration is proposed on wearable jeans material for wide band applications, such as sub-6GHz 5G and WLAN/Wi-Max/Wi-Fi applications. The proposed quad port MIMO antenna is wideband in nature with a frequency range of 2.58 GHz – 6.90 GHz (91.1%) is analyzed by using Ansys HFSS simulator. The wideband MIMO antenna of dual/quad-element is then introduced to address many practical challenges, such as electromagnetic wave scattering, shadowing, and multipath fading. To enhance isolation between radiating elements, antenna blocks are aligned orthogonally to get greater 20 dB isolation over the applications band. Measures of MIMO diversity include the ECC<0.1, DG>9.98, MEG<-6dB and CCL<0.1 bits/s/Hz are found within the acceptable range.

articleTitle: Lightweight Parallel CNN To Classify COVID-19 Associated Pneumonia From Chest X-Ray
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: The global outbreak of the novel Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) has impacted millions of individuals, leading to widespread health, economic, and social consequences. Additionally, the overwhelming number of COVID-19 cases has strained healthcare facilities, underscoring the crucial need for timely and accurate detection of infected individuals to mitigate the pandemic’s impact. Inspired by the fact that existing deep learning models often rely on millions of parameters, rendering them unsuitable for resource-constrained devices, we developed a lightweight Parallel Convolutional Neural Network (PCNN) in this research. The model addresses the necessity for efficient COVID-19 pneumonia diagnostics from chest X-ray images by significantly reducing the number of parameters, resulting in a notable accuracy of 99.25% with 313k parameters. To further reduce parameters, separable convolution blocks were introduced, yielding an accuracy of 99.21% with 224k parameters. Despite their lightweight nature, our model demonstrates competitive performance compared to heavyweight models, emphasizing an accuracy rate of 99.21%. By minimizing computational costs and memory requirements, our model offers a cost-effective solution that can be effortlessly deployed on devices with limited resources.

articleTitle: Finite–Control–Set Model Predictive Control for a Single–Phase Cascaded H–Bridge Multilevel Converter Operating as a Shunt Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper presents a finite-control-set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) for a single-phase cascaded H-bridge (CHB) five-level converter operating as a shunt active power filter (SAPF). Using the MPC scheme in a CHB multilevel converter, a high dynamic performance of the system with reduced harmonic distortion is achieved; but, as the number of output voltage levels increases, the method increases the computational load as a result of a significant number of switching states evaluation, for this reason, in this paper a FCS-MPC scheme is proposed to use a reduced number of switching sets for the control of the multilevel converter and to reduce the computational burden. The discrete model of the system, the generation of the compensation signal, as well as the FCS-MPC algorithm are exposed. Furthermore, to regulate the dc-link voltage, a discrete-time fractional order PI<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup> controller is designed. The simulated results validate the developed control algorithm for the single-phase CHB multilevel converter-based SAPF.

articleTitle: An FPGA-based Automatic Voltage Regulator for a Synchronous Electric Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Voltage control in synchronous generators is done by an excitation system. The exciters are controlled by automatic voltage regulators (AVR), which process the measurement information and execute a control action, dynamically regulating the excitation current to the generator field winding. Therefore, efficient and precise AVR are required to the voltage control. The present work consists of the development of a physical Hardware (AVR) and the internal design of the digital electronics called firmware with a dedicated architecture using hybrid AHDL and VHDL programming, guaranteeing the flexibility and reconfigurability of Intel-FPGA technology to regulate and stabilize efficiently the voltage levels in the synchronous generator. The results of this study show the validation of the Hardware and the own design of the digital electronics of the firmware for the processing and conversions of the internal data. Therefore, the development of the proposed AVR presents validation of reliable data, which will allow us in future works the physical validation of the voltage control in a synchronous generator.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Temperature Gradient System for Phantom Studies in Hyperthermia Therapy
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Hyperthermia therapies are increasingly being used for the control of cancerous tumors in an attempt to maximize the destruction of tumor cells while minimizing the damage to healthy tissues. Accurate temperature management and monitoring is critical due to the non-uniform temperature distributions caused by thermal gradients within the treatment medium. This study presents a comprehensive characterization of an experimental setup designed to replicate temperature gradients observed in clinical hyperthermia treatments. The experimental setup successfully reproduced a temperature gradient ranging from 27 to 60 °C within a phantom model, providing essential quantitative data on the temperature-distance relationship in the target tissue. Linear regression analysis was used to derive an equation describing how temperature depends on the spatial location of the phantom. The results hold great promise for optimizing hyperthermia treatment protocols, enhancing therapeutic efficacy, and improving patient outcomes in clinical practice.

articleTitle: Computing Pseudoinverse Matrices with Single-Layer Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This work evaluates numerical results related to single-layer neural networks, which compute pseudoinverse matrices. This is possible due to the gradient descendent algorithms available in the machine learning TensorFlow framework, which optimizes training processes. Linear algebra principles support our formulations, which are proved at the end of the training stage.

articleTitle: Effect of the CdTe absorber layer’s thickness synthesized by the RF sputtering on the performance of CdTe photovoltaic windows
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: In this work, CdTe thin films were achieved through RF-sputtering at different deposition times (60, 120, 180, 240 min). The structural analysis showed CdTe thin films with cubic and hexagonal phases. In addition, a greater degree of crystallinity can be achieved as a function of the deposition time. SEM characterization indicated the contribution of well- formed and compact grains in the CdTe thin films. Optical properties led to a CdTe bandgap of 1.53 eV. The effects of thermal annealing treatment using CdCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> were also investigated. The maximum efficiency of 4.12% was achieved by optimizing the thickness of the CdTe layer deposited for 60 minutes. It was thermally annealed with CdCl<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The study highlights the importance of optimizing the deposition parameters and thermal annealing treatment to enhance the performance of CdTe solar cells, which could have significant implications for the development of low-cost, high-efficiency semitransparent solar cells.

articleTitle: Semi-automatic grafting machine prototype for tomato seedlings
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Grafting is an important technique in tomato production for improving crop productivity and disease resistance. However, the manual grafting process is time-consuming and labor-intensive. This study presents the development of an automated grafting machine prototype for tomato seedlings to enhance efficiency and graft quality. The prototype incorporates control techniques to perform precise and efficient grafting. Preliminary results indicate that the automated grafting machine could outperform the manual method, reducing the time required for grafting and increasing the overall efficiency and production capacity of a human grafter. This study highlights the potential of automation in tomato grafting, offering a promising solution to enhance crop productivity, reduce labor dependency, and improve sustainability in tomato production. In further work, tests and evaluations will be performed using commercially cultivated tomato seedlings, comparing graft success rates, process duration, and graft quality between the automated machine and the manual method.

articleTitle: IoT Architecture and Security Mecanisms for an Energy Management System in a Smart Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: In this work, we propose a system architecture that allows establishing decentralized control in a direct current (DC) smart microgrid (SMG), using an IoT 2.0 as a frame of reference for the communication between the elements of the digital ecosystem. This system aims to integrate control systems based on machine learning methods running on remote devices, taking advantage of smart systems applied in energy management for an efficient and secure operation of the DC SMG.

articleTitle: Estimation of variations in progesterone in a woman across the menstrual cycle
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: A brain is an organ that can detect shifts in hormone levels. An average woman during a menstrual cycle has fluctuations in some hormones, such as estradiol and progesterone. However it remains poorly understood whether day-to-day fluctuations in this hormones shape human brain dynamics. In these work two series of functional magnetic resonance imaging in resting state (rsfMRI) from a woman during a menstrual cycle were used. The analysis of these series starting from time domain using visibility algorithm to converted these in graphs. The hypothesis is that structure of networks changes with the level of progesterone, and also the geometry of network is affected by the oral contraceptive consume. A healthy woman during a menstrual cycle has fluctuations in some hormones such as estradiol and progesterone; these fluctuations are observable through activation default mode network in functional connectivity maps and are observables through visibility graphs in different stereotaxic cuts in different neuroanatomical planes.

articleTitle: Quaternion Kinematic Observer Using Multiplicative Error
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: In this work we consider a problem of state estimation for a quaternion equation that can be applied to rotation of a rigid body. As measurements we consider coordinates of two or more vectors obtained by quaternionic transformation of fixed vectors. We study both deterministic and stochastic cases. The latter is described by a quaternionic Ito stochastic differential equation. The proof of convergence for the deterministic case is based on the Lyapunov technique. For the stochastic case several expressions for the error covariance equation are derived, and the optimal observer gain minimizing mean quadratic error is calculated.

articleTitle: Hourglass and Semi-Hourglass layout techniques to improve radiation hardening of NMOS devices
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Radiation hardening devices play a critical role in ensuring the reliability and longevity of electronic systems deployed in harsh radiation environments. Over the years, significant advances have been made to enhance the radiation tolerance of electronic components, resulting in improved performance and increased resilience against radiation-induced failures. This paper presents two new layout styles for mosfets the hourglass transistor and the semi-hourglass transistor. The new designs improve the device's behavior under total ionizing radiation (TID). The electrical response of the new devices was characterized by simulations using 3D physical models. The new devices showed 52% and 48% performance in the off-current state after radiation effects.

Author Keywords: positive charge trapped in silicon oxide

articleTitle: Luminescent and electrical properties of PIN diodes based on a-Si1-xCx:H thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This work presents the study of the light emission and conduction mechanisms of PIN diodes using an amorphous silicon-carbide (a-Si1-xCx:H) thin film as active layer. The PIN structures were fabricated by the PECVD technique onto P-type silicon wafers at a substrate temperature of 200 °C. Two different active layers deposited with the CH4/SiH4 flow rates of 30 sccm/ 6sccm and 30 sccm/1 sccm were used. Both structures display red-orange electroluminescence only in forward bias. The structure deposited with a lower silicon content shows a shorter wavelength emission with a higher intensity at a lower voltage bias. From the current-voltage measurements the dominant charge transport mechanisms were proposed. On the one hand, the Fowler-Nordheim tunneling was related to the highest silicon content structure due to a lower barrier height, and on the other hand, the trap-assisted tunneling was associated with the lowest silicon content related to a higher density of defects in localized tail states.

articleTitle: Digital Signal Transmission Through a Short-Reach Optical Link Using an FPGA Card
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper describes the experimental digital signal transmission through a short-reach optical link of 100 m using an FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) development card. The use of an FPGA development card allows to process in a friendly way the information to be transmitted, as well as, an easy reconfiguration. This characteristic constitutes the originality of this work. The transmission is carried out in baseband and the performance metric to evaluate this approach is carried out by determining the Mean Square Error (MSE) and the eye diagram. Potentially, this proposal can be used to connect short links in data centers.

articleTitle: Stress Detection Protocol in Vehicular Driving using Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Stress is a physiological response that prepares the body to face adversities and chronic exposure to stressful events and, it can lead to health deterioration and chronic illnesses. Driving in congested areas or during peak hours is a daily stressful event for residents in Mexico City. Biosignals, such as electrodermal activity, electroencephalography, photopletismography, and skin temperature, are known to reflect physiological changes related to stress. In this study, a research protocol was developed to provoke stress states associated with driving using a virtual reality environment. The protocol was applied to 17 participants, generating a database of physiological signals. The data set has been characterized using descriptive statistics. This database could be used to detect stress levels using artificial intelligence in future studies.

articleTitle: Control System for Vibration Attenuation in a Flexible Beam
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This work focuses on designing a control system for vibration attenuation in cantilever beam structures. These structures are widely used in various industries but are prone to vibrations that can lead to structural deformations, system failures, and increased energy consumption. To address these issues, we propose a velocity feedback-based control approach that targets a non-fading periodic disturbance matching the critical natural frequency of the cantilever beam. A prototype was constructed, and experimental tests were conducted to validate the proposed control approach. Modal identification methods were employed to determine the parameters of the instrumented beam, and simulation studies were performed to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed controller. Finally, the controller was implemented on the physical prototype. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed controller in attenuating vibrations, with more significant improvements observed in simulation compared to physical experiments.

articleTitle: Study on the optoelectronic properties of the heterostructure ZnO/CdS/CdTe for its applications in CdTe solar cells
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This work focuses on the development of a photovoltaic cell based on the CdS/CdTe heterostructure, the incorporation of a high resistivity ZnO layer was proposed, which could reduce the interfacial current density between the front contact and CdS in the device. CdS films on glass/SnO₂:F/ZnO substrates were obtained by chemical bath technique by varying the precursors concentrations. Subsequently, CdTe film was deposited on glass/SnO₂:F/ZnO/CdS heterostructure by close space sublimation to obtain an n-p union solar cell. Structural and optoelectronic characterization allowed the determination of the critical growth parameters under which the CdS film's properties were improved. Structural characterization performed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and Raman spectroscopy suggests that CdS films have a mixture of cubic and hexagonal phases. CdS films have an optical transmittance maximum of 80%, in the visible region. Electrical measurements confirm the n-type conductivity of the CdS films. For the CdTe film, the cubic phase was identified by XRD. Raman characterization showed modes attributed to a Te-rich surface due to the thermal treatment. The device efficiency increases by 2% with the incorporation of a ZnO high resistive layer compared to the reference cells.

articleTitle: CMOS Design of a Memristor Emulator: Model, Simulation and Results
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper presents a memristor emulator constructed with active building blocks and a model based on port equations. The proposed memristor emulator employs analog current-mode building blocks such as the current follower (CF), an operational transconductance amplifier (OTA), and a passive element. The circuit and model exhibit the characteristics inherent to a memristor. The memristor emulator can be configured as either decremental or incremental and demonstrates satisfactory performance up to frequencies of 20 MHz. To validate the functionality of the proposed circuit, simulations were performed using Cadence software and TSMC’s 180 nm technology. The simulations were conducted under typical operating conditions with a supply voltage of ±1.2 V.

articleTitle: Stabilization of a DC-DC buck converter for photovoltaic MPPT applications
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of an input-output linearization controller combined with a proportional integral retarded (PIR) control acting as a maximum power point tracking (MPPT) technique for photovoltaic (PV) panels. The approach utilizes a DC-DC buck converter and the well-known perturb and observe maximum power searching algorithm. The MPPT system aims to extract the maximum power from a photo-voltaic module (PVM) when faced with environmental variations such as changes in irradiance and temperature. Simulation results illustrate the effectiveness of the developed method.

articleTitle: Optimal Risk Sensitive Controller Design Applied to a Stochastic Dynamics of a Simple Pendulum Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: In this paper the Risk-Sensitive (RS) Optimal Controller Equations for Polynomial Stochastic Systems of first degree with tuning in the real states are applied to the of simple pendulum model. This RS controller contains the RS optimal control equations and the RS filtering equations connecting the control into the estimate RS equations. The dynamic of the state contains a parameter ϵ, as attenuation of the noise and parameter γ which permits adjustment to the gain control values to obtain solution in R. Values of the exponential quadratic cost criterion function are obtained for some values of parameter ϵ, which are selected according to the real tolerance of the motor of the pendulum. Results (errors values, exponential quadratic cost criterion values) presented in a table show the feasibility of this proposal.

articleTitle: Classification of EEG signals from Imagined Hand Movements based on a Model of Executed Movements
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the classification of EEG signals from imagined hand movements using an artificial intelligence model trained on real movements. The study is based on the hypothesis that imagined movements elicit similar neuronal activation as real movements but with a peripheral blockade that prevents physical execution. The study uses a Support Vector Machine (SVM) with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel to classify the EEG signals captured by an Aura Neurotech device. The study achieves a classification accuracy of 69% for imagined and real movements, suggesting that this approach is feasible and has implications for the development of more intuitive and effective brain-computer interfaces.

articleTitle: Characterization Of Physiological Signals Under Cognitive Stress
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: A fusion of wearable device sensors and an electroencephalography system was implemented to identify changes under controlled situations related to stress in the student’s population, to assess whether the physiological signals can detect variations in the stress level by a descriptive statistical analysis. The signals used are: movement, blood volume pulse, electrodermal activity, heart rate, temperature and electroencephalography. The analysis was made in volunteers between 18 and 25 years old, who are young adults with at least 10 years of schooling and being apparently healthy. The recording protocol consisted of 3 consecutive stages taken in a single session, which consisted of two math tests (stage 1 and stage 3) with a relaxation period (stage 2) in between. The physiological signal data were segmented per stage and descriptive statistical metrics were calculated per volunteer. For the appropriate proper selection of metrics, they were compared using the Repeated Measures one-way ANOVA method with α = 0.05, using Tukey's multiple comparisons tests. It was found that the heart rate and temperature signals, along with the descriptive statistical metrics, range, and kurtosis, are the best suited for the study to find the differences. Volunteers in stage 3 maintained a state of relaxation equal to or less than that of stage 2.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network-Based Control and FCS-MPC for DC/DC and CHB Multilevel Converters for PV Water Pumping Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper explains an artificial neural network (ANN)-based control for photovoltaic (PV) system with dc/dc boost converters connected in cascaded with a single-phase cascaded H-bridge (CHB) 9-level inverter with finite control set (FCS) model predictive control (MPC) for rural water pumping with speed control. First, a digital PI controller for each of the four boost converters is designed, then this controller is used as a supervisor to train the ANN, which is designed with the help of Matlab/Simulink software. Once each dc-bus voltage is regulated, the CHB 9-level inverter with the FCS-MPC algorithm is utilized to control the current and the speed of an induction motor water pump. The simulation results show that the ANN-based control scheme for the boost converters improves the voltage control performance compared to the PI, and an excellent behavior of the water pump is achieved with the FCS-MPC scheme developed for the CHB multilevel inverter

articleTitle: Design and simulation of a MIMO octagonal-shape hybrid transparent-metallic film antenna for Ultra-Wideband systems
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This article presents the design of an octagonal-shaped hybrid transparent-metallic film patch two-port antenna for ultra-wideband systems. A C-band transparent antenna design was obtained, in which the ground plane and the feedline have been modified. According to simulation results of the reflection coefficient, this antenna has a bandwidth between 2.4 and 12 GHz. The radiation pattern of the antenna was obtained by simulation points to an omnidirectional operation, with an average gain of -3 dB at 3.3 GHz. The simulated Envelop Correlation Coefficient points to an isolated operation between ports, with a top value of 0.44 at 4 GHz. The characterization of Diversity Gain also refers to an independent operation between ports, with a minimal value of 8.93. Meanwhile, closer to the obtained radiation coefficients, the Total Active Reflection Coefficient shows values below -10 dB in the frequency range between 2.7 and 12 GHz. Due to these characteristics, this antenna improves the gain. It is easier to fabricate than other transparent antennas and it can still be easily integrated in places like window frames or in another environment where there is mandatory Line-of-Sight communication or discrete implementations.

articleTitle: New Cascade Observer for a Class of Nonlinear Systems with Time-delayed Outputs
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper presents a new cascade structure for the estimation of the delay-free state vector for a class of nonlinear systems with long time-delay output. The base in the cascade observer is a standard high-gain observer to estimate the delayed state vector, and this new cascade presents the redesign of the subsystems present in the cascade compensating in a time horizon the delay of the system output, achieving the estimation of the delay-free state vector. Sufficient conditions are proposed to establish that the observation error exponentially converges to zero. The performance of the proposed observer is evaluated by considering as example an uncertain nonlinear system with long time-delayed output.

articleTitle: An Extended Generalized Super-Twisting Algorithm for Estimating Key Biochemical Variables in Bioprocesses
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: In order to improve the behavior of any bioprocess, it is required to know some of its key biochemical variables, such as the reaction rates and the influent feeding rates. However, these variables are hard to measure, challenging to describe mathematically, or can be the source of unknown disturbances. Moreover, even though many unknown input observers were designed for their estimation, their convergence cannot be modified. In this work, an extended generalized super-twisting algorithm is designed to simultaneously estimate reaction rates and influent feeding rates in finite time. For this task, a change of variables is used, valid if the dilution rate is strictly positive. The proposed algorithm is applied on an alcoholic fermentation process, and simulated results show a good performance from the design observer.

articleTitle: Slew-rate Comparison of single-ended amplifiers-the Folded Cascode and the Recycling Folded Cascode
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: In this paper, two cascode amplifiers are analyzed. For comparison purposes, same design specifications were used to size them by using the g<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> methodology (CMOS 130 nm). In this analysis, slew-rate is the target because settling time strongly depends on it. Corners-based simulations were carried out to assess the process variations effect on the amplifiers performance. From this study the recycling folded cascode amplifier gives the highighest value and is more tolerant to process variations.

articleTitle: Mechanical Activity Associated with Gastric Pacemaker
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: The Surface Electrogastrography (sEGG) technique has previously been used to evaluate gastric disorders, but little has been explored in the analysis of the gastric pacemaker signal and its relationship to higher frequency components. This article describes the methodology developed to determine the percentage of mechanical activity about gastric pacing in Electrogastrography (EGG) signals. Unipolar 6-channel EGG data were acquired and processed from a control group composed of 58 subjects and from 23 patients with Type II Diabetes Mellitus, at three different states: fasting, water, and nourishment. In this study, we have implemented an algorithm that takes advantage of signals from a previously reported database, applying the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) and using daubechies4 (db4) as mother wavelet. This allows us to separate the gastric mechanical activity bands, filtering and identifying the peaks and valleys of the signal to obtain a percentage association of mechanical activity according to group, state, and channel. The results show that there is a relationship between the position of the electrodes, the state in which it is located, and that it is consistent throughout the sample considered. Besides, channel 2 was capable to identify the difference between the two groups along all states.

articleTitle: Improved Photoluminescence Intensity of Silicon Rich Oxide Film by Surface Etching
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Silicon rich oxide (SRO) films are a promising material to develop silicon-based light sources, a key device in Silicon Photonics. Nevertheless, it has been experimentally shown that a surface oxide layer is formed on the SRO films after a thermal annealing process, which possibly does not contribute to light emission. Then, in this work, the effect of wet etching steps (different depths) on the morphological and photoluminescent (PL) properties of SRO films is studied. Two SRO films with different Si-excess, labeled as SRO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> and SRO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>, were deposited by low pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD) using N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O and SiH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> as the reactive gasses. Subscript 5 and 10 indicates the gas flow ratio (Ro)=N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O/SiH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>. The initial thickness of both SRO films is about 80 nm. An improvement of the PL intensity is observed when the thickness of SRO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> and SRO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> films is 37.30 ± 2.60 and 31.73 ± 0.55 nm, respectively. Using the maximum emission wavelength and average roughness, it was verified that the SRO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> film present silicon nanoparticles with a larger size than the SRO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> film. Finally, atomic force microscopy reveals the presence of some peaks on the surface of SRO films. The density of these peaks increases after the last etching step in both films. This could indicate the formation of Si-nanopyramid structures at the SRO/Si-substrate interface. Our results show that the surface oxidation plays an important role in the PL quenching.

articleTitle: Synthesis and characterization of ZnS films deposited by spray pyrolysis
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)

authors.preferredName: María de la Luz Olvera Amador

abstract: In this work, the crystallographic, morphological and optical properties of ZnS films synthesized by the spray pyrolysis method were analyzed, using rosemary extracts in the preparation of the starting solution. The ZnS films were deposited at 350 °C and different deposition times (1-4 min). The crystallographic properties were determined by X-ray diffraction, where the cubic phase of ZnS was confirmed. In the films that did not add rosemary, the presence of an elemental Zn phase was observed, while the films deposited with different percentages of rosemary extract (5, 15, 25 and 50%) only presented the cubic ZnS phase. The scanning electron microscopy, SEM, images of the films synthesized with rosemary extract showed particles with spherical morphology and small particle sizes that depend on the concentration of the extract, with formation of agglomerates due to the presence of organic compounds from the extract. The bandgap energies (Eg) for the ZnS films without extract ranged from 3.2 to 3.4 eV, while the films deposited with extract presented a significant decrease in their Eg of 1.2-3.2 eV, this due to organic molecules deposited on the ZnS surface. The presence of these organic species was confirmed by infrared spectroscopy. These materials presented good crystallographic, structural, surface and optical properties, results that are promising for applications such as solar cells and heterogeneous photocatalysis.

articleTitle: A Novel Fractional Order Differentiator
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: The aim of this study is to analyze and design a novel fractional order differentiator which is robust against noise, this method allows to estimate the Caputo fractional order derivative of an unknown bounded noisy signal, also the original signal is estimated. In this sense, our proposal can reduce the effect of noise in the estimation of the original signal as well as in its fractional order derivative. The construction of this differentiator is based on a simple proportional-fractional order integral algorithm. Numerical simulations are performed considering the presence and absence of noise, showing the effectiveness, accuracy and robustness of our fractional order differentiator.

articleTitle: Study of the properties of FZO thin films deposited by USP using a milled Zn precursor
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)

authors.preferredName: M. de la L. Olvera A

abstract: Zinc oxide thin films doped with fluorine (FZO) were deposited by the ultrasonic chemical spray technique. Different starting solutions from unmilled and milled Zn precursor were prepared, and then FZO films were deposited on soda-lime substrates. For milling the precursors, a planetary ball mill opered at constant speed and time, 500 rpm and 60 min, respectively, was used. FZO films were processed at constant deposition temperature, 450°C, and two deposition times, 8 and 14 min. The results reveal that, under the same deposition parameters, the electrical properties of FZO thin films deposited from milled precursor are better than those obtained for films deposited from starting solutions prepared from unmilled precursors.X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed that all films spectra fit well with the hexagonal wurtzite structure, presenting a preferential orientation along the (002) planes. The surface morphology characterization, carried out by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), showed changes with the milling process of the Zn precursor, passing from a triangular-shaped grains with unmilled precursors to thin sheets with hexagonal shapes with those milled. The use of a grinded precursor to prepare the starting solutions to deposit FZO thin films by the USP technique influences their physical properties.

articleTitle: Optical and Electrical Properties of Annealed AZO/Ag/AZO Multilayer Deposited Using RF Sputtering Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This work aims at analyzing the effect of both Ag middle layer and annealing effects on the structural, optical and electrical properties of Al-doped ZnO (AZO) thin-films. In this framework, AZO/Ag/AZO tri-layers were deposited on glass substrates using RF magnetron sputtering technique. Structural, optical and electrical characterizations were carried out using XRD, UV-Vis Spectrophotometry and Hall measurements, respectively. The obtained XRD patterns demonstrated the enhanced crystallinity of the annealed AZO/Ag/AZO multilayer structure. In addition, transmittance spectra of prepared samples revealed the enhanced visible transparency of the annealed structure, showing a high average transparency of 85%. It is found also that the use of annealing and Ag middle layer can enlarge the band gap (3.53 eV). This is attributed to the increase of the free charge carrier, which can shift the Fermi Level. Electrical characterizations demonstrate that annealing process can modulate the electrical properties of the AZO/Ag/AZO thin-film, offering a high mobility of 17 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Vs and a favorable sheet-resistance of 46 Ω/eq. Therefore, the present study can provide guidelines for the fabrication of alternative buffer layer, which can be appropriate for various thin-film solar cell technologies.

articleTitle: G and GO interaction into TiO2 (010) anatase and its influence on the bandgap: DFT Study
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: In this work, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to investigate the effect of graphene (G) and graphene oxide (GO) on the electronic properties of TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. Initially, a bandgap of 3.23 eV was determined for pure anatase TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layers. Subsequently, with the incorporation of G and GO, a possible hybridization effect of the electron states at the interface was observed, leading to the formation of new intermediate energy bands not originally found in TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. This condition causes the bandgap of the hybrid material to be reduced. Our calculations further showed how both structures interact with the TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> surface, providing valuable information that offers opportunities to optimize the interfaces and improve the performance of these materials in various applications.

articleTitle: Significance of the substrate temperature on the physical properties of RF sputtered Sb2Te3 thin films
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Sb2Te3 thin films were grown by RF magnetron sputtering at a substrate temperature of 300 °C and 350 °C. The structural, morphological, optical and electrical properties were evaluated as a function of the substrate temperature. The structural analysis revealed that the thin films exhibited diffraction planes and Raman modes attributed to the rhombohedral phase of Sb2Te3. The results from the optical characterization indicated that the Sb2Te3 samples function exceptionally well as an absorber layer in the UV-Vis region. According to the morphological study, the thin films grew with densely packed grains, each measuring around 100 nm in size. A high carrier concentration on the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> and a low electrical resistivity in the range of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> Ω∙cm were obtained in the Sb2Te3 material.

articleTitle: FPGA Simulation for Computing Pseudoinverse Matrices
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Many scientific and engineering processing models of big data deal with classification tasks. In particular, current intelligent approaches work efficiently for them, as they use neural techniques with shallow architectures. The Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), which is a one-hidden layer feedforward neural network, is capable of achieving high accuracy in these tasks. Moreover, one of its weighting matrices is the pseudoinverse of the hidden data. In this sense, this work presents meaningful results of computing the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse for the ELM, using a recurrent model. The numerical simulations were based on an FPGA framework used to design a pseudoinverse-computing core.

articleTitle: Detection and Classification of Heart Arrhythmias by Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: The arrythmias are found frequently in patients and it could be an indicator of cardiovascular diseases or an immediate health danger. This is why it is important to identify and classify correctly these irregularities in the heartbeat. The present paper proposes the architecture and evaluates the performance of a 1D convolutional neural network capable of classifying ECG signals in five classes, four types of arrythmias and one considered as normal. The five classes were first balanced and then separeted in 70% and 30% for training and testing, respectively. Metrics were calculated for each of the five classes: precision, recall, specificity and F1 score. The mininum value obtained was 0.97 in recall for the normal class, and the maximum was 0.99 for the specificity of all the classes and most of the other metrics.

articleTitle: Distributed Predefined-Time Optimization for Basic Source Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper introduces a distributed optimization algorithm for achieving formation control in multi-agent systems utilizing the zero-gradient sum property and the predefined-time stabilization framework. The distributed optimization scheme offers the flexibility to assign the settling time according to desired requirements, distinguishing it from existing finite and fixed-time schemes. Moreover, the algorithm eliminates the need for agents to exchange local gradients or Hessians of the cost functions. The algorithm’s effectiveness is validated through an application to a basic case of distributed source localization.

articleTitle: Identification and Control Design for an Experimental Setup to Take Home
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: From classroom experience arises a necessity to demonstrate control outcomes through physical examples. One option to carry out these experiments is by using electronics to implement systems, along with microcontrollers to handle data acquisition and control tasks. In this study, a system that generates heat by passing current through the collector-emitter of a power transistor is implemented. The current flow is regulated by a PWM signal applied to the base. A temperature sensor is constructed using a thermistor, which provides feedback on the temperature and compares it to a reference value. The control scheme is implemented using an affordable microcontroller. Input-output measurements for open-loop process identification are performed using the same microcontroller with the support of a Python program. The results are presented to facilitate DIY implementation and to aid in better understanding of various concepts.

articleTitle: A New Gate-Trench Junctionless SiC Power MOSFET: Performance Assessement and Circuit Level Investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This work aims at analyzing the effect of combining Junctionless (JL) technology and gate-trench strategy for improving the electrical and switching performances of SiC power MOSFET devices. The device is modeled using numerical approaches to assess its performance for power electronic applications. It is found that the proposed device can allow achieving higher derived current capability and maintains low off-state current. In addition, the proposed gate-trench JL MOSFET demonstrates improved on-resistance and high breakdown characteristics, resulting in a superior Figure-of-Merit (FoM) value of BV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/Ron= 2580 MV/mΩ.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>. To analyze the switching characteristics of the proposed transistor, the device is implemented in an inverter-gate circuit. It is shown that the analyzed power-MOSFET using combined JL and gate-trench aspects offers improved switching performances with low noise margin effects. Therefore, the proposed gate-trench JL MOSFET can address the trade-off between high breakdown characteristics and improved switching properties, suggesting it as a potential cost-effective alternative transistor for power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Multi-label Bengali Abusive Comments Classification using Problem Transformation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Sentiment analysis on the Bengali language is limited to binary and multi-class classifications. This paper focuses on the multi-label classification of the Bengali abusive social media comments dataset having 10220 rows of different social media negative comments using the problem transformation method. The texts are categorized into five labels: toxic, threat, obscene, insult, and racism. Three different multi-label approaches: Binary Relevance, Label Powerset, and Classifier Chain combined with three popular machine learning algorithms: Multinomial Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression are implemented in this research. This study evaluates the performance of these models by applying them to various classification scenarios, considering five-label, four-label, three-label, and two-label classifications independently. Our research outcomes are evaluated with some performance indicators: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Scores, Confusion matrix, Macro-average, and Hamming score. The combination of Label Powerset and Logistic Regression outperformed the other two classifier-model combinations because of their quick adaptation to the dataset with an accuracy of 88.07% for five label classifications, 90.12% for four label classifications, 90.56% considering three label classifications and 92.67% for two label classification individually. With 88.07% accuracy, the Label Powerset with Logistic Regression approach can be applied to classify five types of sentiment in a single text.

articleTitle: Ultrasonically sprayed undoped and indium-doped titanium oxide thin films for methylene blue degradation: Effect of molarity and irradiation time
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Undoped and Indium- 3 at % doped titanium oxide thin films were deposited at 450 °C by ultrasonic spray pyrolysis technique on glass substrates. The molarity content in the starting solution was varied from 0.1 to 0.2 M to study its effect on the degradation of methylene blue (MB) dye in the photocatalytic process. X-ray diffraction patterns confirm the anatase structure of TiO2. A maximum MB degradation of about 60 % was achieved for a UV light exposition time of 210 min. The degradation behavior with respect to UV exposition time showed a linear relationship with the concentration of charge carriers, which is explicated in this work. The indium doped titanium oxide thin films deposited with 0.2 M are relatively more promising for MB degradation when the UV exposure times are larger than 120 min.

articleTitle: Performance assessment of a new optimized Junctionless SiSn MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Junctionless Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistor (JL MOSFET) has attracted more consideration due to its simple fabrication process and improved performances. Moreover, this transistor is suitable for high scalability and low-power nanoelectronic applications. However, the low drift current (ON-state current) provided by this device and the degraded switching characteristics are the major issues that needs to be overcome. In this context, this work aims to propose a new design paradigm based on combined junctionless design and global metaheuristic optimization technique to improve the SiSn transistor performances for deep submicron microelectronic applications. It is demonstrated that the proposed design framework paves the way for the circuit designers not only to identify the appropriate materials for high drift current values, but also to realize high-performance transistors with high-speed commutation and low-power consumption, which are considered as important Figures-of-Merit (FoMs) for digital and analog integrated circuits applications. The developed approach based on combining the proposed junctionless structure with global metaheuristic optimization can open new paths for the design of high-performance and low-cost microelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Polyvinylidene Fluoride Membranes as Force Detectors for Bruxism Behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper presents the application of polyvinylidene fluoride PVDF membranes as bite force sensors for monitoring masticatory activity associated with bruxism behavior. Bruxism refers to the clenching or grinding of teeth, which can lead to various orofacial problems. The proposed application of PVDF membranes aims to provide a method for quantitatively measuring bite force in a model of masticatory activity. This paper is part of a work in progress that seeks to establish a correlation between the manifestation of bruxism episodes and the detection of characteristic clinical patterns by analyzing the frequency response of PVDF membranes at different pressures.

articleTitle: Copper-Doped Tin Oxide Thin Films Prepared by Sol-Gel Dip Coating Technique for CO Gas Sensing
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)

authors.preferredName: María De La Luz Olvera Amador

abstract: Copper-doped tin oxide (Cu: SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) thin films have been fabricated using the sol-gel dip coating technique with one, two, and three immersion cycles. This study aimed to investigate the influence of the number of immersion cycles on the structural, morphological, and optical properties of the films for their potential application in CO gas sensing. The thin films were characterized by means of electronic microscopies (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) studies, and UV-Vis’s spectroscopy. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis studies the film's crystalline structure and phase purity. The SEM images showed that the films had a uniform and dense structure, with an increase in the number of immersion cycles. UV-Vis spectroscopy was conducted to investigate the optical properties of the films. Gas sensing measurements were performed to evaluate the CO gas sensing performance of the films. The results demonstrated that the films prepared with three immersion cycles exhibited the highest sensitivity (1137.70) to CO gas.

articleTitle: Towards Breast Cancer Treatment Planning by Microwave Ablation Via Tumor Characterization Using Medoid-based Eigenvectors
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: One of the most promising therapies for breast cancer treatment is microwave ablation (MWA). Nevertheless, it is necessary to design personalized treatment planning to ensure the correct application of this technique. The MWA-based treatment planning characterizes the tumor’s geometry, generates an adequate applicator configuration, and computes electromagnetic (EM) and thermal models to look for efficient tumor ablation. This work is focused on the first step of the treatment planning, analyzing 22 digital breast tumor models through the Principal Components Analysis (PCA) method, obtaining the eigenvectors and eigenvalues using the medoid of the tumor to ensure an existing point that can be reachable by the microwave applicators. This medoid-based approach is compared with the information obtained using the centroid of the tumor. The results show that the maximum distance between the centroid and the medoid and the maximum distance of the eigenvalues are approximately 1 mm, and the maximum difference between the angle of the eigenvectors is approximately 4°. Considering that the safety margin for the tumors in surgery or ablation is between 5 and 10 mm, the maximum distance is lower than this range; hence, the centroid can be replaced with the medoid to obtain the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors to characterize the tumor.

articleTitle: Building Hierarchical Workflow Nets for Discrete-Event Processes Discovery
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: This paper presents a method to build hierarchical workflow nets (WFN) from a log of event traces representing the behavior of a discrete event process. The proposed method operates in two phases: event bundling, and model construction. The bundling of events is performed according to traces of the event log. The event alphabet is partitioned into clusters called Ordered Execution Sets (OES), in which all the events in the class always occur together in the same traces of the event log; besides, the cluster contains a unique subset of concurrent events. Afterwards, the two-level hierarchical WFN is constructed. For every OESj, a Petri Net (PN) substructure is built according to the causal and concurrent relations between events in the bund; each substructure is net of level two represented by a macro-transition within the net of level one. Macro-transitions are linked through places following simple rules that consider the boundary events of the OES substructures. The algorithms derived from the method, which have polynomial-time complexity, have been implemented and tested on artificial event logs.

articleTitle: Detection and Characterization of Focused Ultrasonic Field using Schlieren Effect and Continuous Laser
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: The Schlieren effect, commonly used in the acoustics field, allows for the detection and characterization of ultrasonic fields by taking advantage of the alteration in the refractive index that occurs when an acoustic wave induces changes in the pressure and density of a medium. In this study, a different approach is proposed for detecting and quantifying a focused ultrasonic field using a continuous laser as an emitter and a photodiode as a receiver, modulating the laser position along the ultrasonic field induced in a controlled medium. The measurements carried out in the laboratory presented variations in the laser intensity correlated with proximity to the focus, observing a maximum reduction of 11.02% in the area of highest pressure. Such reductions vary depending on the induced pressures in the medium. This methodology proposed an alternative approach for the detection and characterization of the acoustic field in medicine, relating the variation in laser intensity with the pressure of an ultrasonic field. Additionally, because the experimental design employed, it facilitates the detection of ultrasonic fields compared to conventional techniques.

articleTitle: Methodology for the implementation of Memristor models in FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 20th International Conference on Electrical Engineering, Computing Science and Automatic Control (CCE)
abstract: Storing information and gradually modifying its electrical resistance are some of the most important qualities of the memristor. According to the importance generated by this new device, a methodology for the implementation of memristor models in hardware based on field programmable gate arrays (FPGA) is proposed. This will allow the development of new applications in several areas such as: signal processing, computer vision, neuromorphic computing, among others, demonstrating the effectiveness of the methodology and the potential of this new technology. The methodology consists of three main steps: validation of the memristor models, description of the hardware components and the testing of models. In addition the final performace in terms of resource consumption and computational complexity is also shown.
